item.title: The Kamo River: Kyoto's Riverside Promenade — Guide
item.description: The Kamogawa, the Kamo River, runs north to south through the middle of Kyoto and is the city’s best-loved outdoor space, a long ribbon of grassy banks, paths and stepping-stone crossings threading the centre. Locals come here to jog, cycle, picnic, play music and simply sit — famously in evenly spaced couples along the water at Shijo. In summer, restaurants along the west bank at Pontocho and Kiyamachi build kawadoko, wooden dining platforms out over the river, for open-air meals in the evening cool.
